Describe an exposure data source

Source: R/sources.R
svy_exposure.Rd

Wraps the exposure data you have, so that svy_expose() can link it to people. Four kinds of source are supported:

Usage

svy_exposure(
  x,
  type = c("auto", "raster", "points", "grid", "areas"),
  value = "value",
  date = "date",
  unit = "id",
  lon = "lon",
  lat = "lat",
  crs = 4326,
  step = c("auto", "day", "month", "year", "layer"),
  agg_fun = c("mean", "median", "max", "min", "sum"),
  dates = NULL,
  static = FALSE,
  boundaries = NULL,
  boundary_id = NULL
)

Arguments

x

A SpatRaster, a data frame, or a file path.

type

One of "auto", "raster", "points", "grid", "areas".

value, date

Column names of the exposure value and its date or timestamp (tables only).

unit

Column naming the monitor or area (tables). Not needed for grid, where cells are identified by their coordinates.

lon, lat

Coordinate columns (points and grid).

crs

Coordinate reference system of lon/lat. Default WGS84.

step

Length of one period: "auto" (infer from the dates), "day", "month", "year", or "layer" (each date lasts until the next, for irregular series such as 8-day composites). Sub-daily table data are always aggregated to days.

agg_fun

How to combine several readings in one period of a table: "mean" (default), "median", "max", "min" or "sum".

dates

For rasters: the date of each layer. If NULL, taken from terra::time(), then from dates in the layer names such as pm25_2019-03 or pm25_20190305.

static

TRUE for a raster with no time dimension (for example population density or distance to road). Every window then receives the same value.

boundaries

Optional sf polygons for areas, used to find which area each person lives in.

boundary_id

Column in boundaries holding the unit identifier that matches unit.

Value

An object of class svy_exposure_source.

Details

  • raster: a SpatRaster, or a file path. One layer per time step (daily, monthly, annual or irregular), or a single static layer.

  • points: a table of monitor or sensor readings with one row per monitor and time: an identifier, longitude, latitude, a date and a value. Sub-daily timestamps are aggregated to days first.

  • grid: a table of regular grid cells in the same long format as points (for example a raster exported to CSV). Cells are treated as monitors at the cell centres.

  • areas: a table of values for administrative units (district, region) and dates, with no coordinates. People are matched to a unit by a column in their data, or by boundaries, a polygon layer.

Tables can be a data frame or a path to a .csv, .csv.gz or .parquet file. The type is detected from the columns unless you set type.

Examples

# Monitor readings
readings <- data.frame(
  monitor = rep(c("A", "B"), each = 3),
  lon = rep(c(-0.20, -0.18), each = 3), lat = 5.6,
  date = rep(as.Date("2020-01-01") + 0:2, 2),
  pm25 = c(30, 32, 31, 50, 52, 51)
)
svy_exposure(readings, unit = "monitor", value = "pm25")
#> <svy_exposure_source>: points
#> • Time step: day; 3 periods, 2020-01-01 to 2020-01-03
#> • 2 unit(s); 100% of unit-periods have a value
